title: An Image Analysis Pipeline to Quantify Cracks in Materials or Adhesion Defects in Tissues
author: Stéphane Verger
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Acquire suitable images
steps.instruction: Capture 2‑D grayscale images with a confocal microscope (or any imaging system) that show a strong pixel‑intensity contrast between cells (or material) and the cracks, and where each crack forms a closed domain; obtain Z‑stacks if needed and project them to 2‑D (e.g., Fiji → Image → Stacks → Z Project → Max Intensity).

steps.title: Pre‑process images in Fiji
steps.instruction: Prepare each image for the analysis pipeline by converting to 8‑bit, selecting the correct channel, optionally enhancing contrast, smoothing with a median filter, and determining a suitable threshold.

substeps.instruction: Load the 2‑D image in Fiji.
Convert to 8‑bit: Image → Type → 8‑bit.
If the image is multichannel, split channels and keep the appropriate one: Image → Color → Split Channels.
Optionally enhance contrast: Process → Enhance Contrast… → set “Saturated pixels” to 0.3 %.
Smooth the image with a median filter: Process → Filters → Median… → set radius (e.g., 3 pixels) to reduce noise without excessive blurring.
Open the Threshold tool (Image → Adjust → Threshold…) and adjust the threshold until the cracks are cleanly separated from the background (example threshold value 162).
Save the processed image as .tif or .jpg (File → Save As → Tiff… or JPEG…) and append “_XXXthld” to the filename, where XXX is the three‑digit threshold value used (e.g., sample_1_162thld.tif).

steps.title: Organize image folders
steps.instruction: Create a main directory (referred to as “updir”) that contains sub‑directories for each experimental group (e.g., different mutants or growth conditions); place all pre‑processed images in the appropriate sub‑folders.

steps.title: Install Miniconda and dependencies
steps.instruction: Set up a Python 2.7 environment with all required packages using Miniconda.

substeps.instruction: Download the Miniconda installer:
• Linux: wget https://repo.continuum.io/miniconda/Miniconda2-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh
• macOS: wget https://repo.continuum.io/miniconda/Miniconda2-latest-MacOSX-x86_64.sh
• Windows: download the .exe installer from the official Miniconda website.
Install Miniconda:

• Linux/macOS: open a terminal, cd to the download folder (e.g., cd ~/Downloads), run bash Miniconda2-latest‑Linux‑x86_64.sh (or the macOS script), then delete the installer with rm Miniconda2‑latest‑Linux‑x86_64.sh (or the macOS equivalent).
• Windows: run the .exe, choose an install location (e.g., C:\Users\<name>\.miniconda), and answer YES when prompted to add conda to PATH.
Test the installation by opening a new terminal and typing: conda
Download the analysis repository from GitHub (click “Clone or download” → Download ZIP) and extract the folder “cell_separation_analysis‑master”.
In a terminal, navigate to the extracted folder: cd path/to/Cell_separation_analysis-master/
Create the conda environment with the provided YAML file: conda env create -f cell-sep-env.yml
Activate the environment each time you wish to run the analysis: source activate cell-sep-env

steps.title: Verify installation with test data
steps.instruction: Confirm that the script runs correctly on the supplied test images.

substeps.instruction: Launch IPython: ipython
Within IPython, change to the repository folder: cd path/to/Cell_separation_analysis-master/
Run the script: %run Cell_separation_analysis.py
Check that output files are created in the “Test_files” sub‑directory.

steps.title: Configure analysis parameters
steps.instruction: Edit the “Cell_separation_analysis.py” file to set the parameters that match your data.

substeps.instruction: Open Cell_separation_analysis.py in a text editor.
Locate the “parameters” section (contains 7 entries).
Set the image directory (updir) – either a full path (e.g., /home/user/updir/) or a relative path (./updir/).
Enter the pixel size in microns (obtain from Fiji: Image → Properties → Pixel width/height).
Define minimum and maximum crack area in pixel units (e.g., min_area_of_crack = 50, max_area_of_crack = 10000).
Choose the threshold type: “min” for bright cracks or “max” for dark cracks.
If desired, enable global analyses by changing Global_Output_Size and Global_Polarhist_output from False to True.
Save the file.

steps.title: Run the analysis on your images
steps.instruction: Execute the script with the configured parameters to quantify cracks.

substeps.instruction: In a terminal with the conda environment active, start IPython: ipython
Navigate to the repository folder if not already there: cd path/to/Cell_separation_analysis-master/
Run the script: %run Cell_separation_analysis.py
The program will process all images found in the organized folder hierarchy and write results to the corresponding output files.
